body.name: \(p(P')\) and \(\omega(P')\)
body.construction: On the binary-treatment inference submodel \(\mathcal A=\{d,e\}\), every candidate law \(P'\) has \(P'\{D\in\{d,e\}\}=1\). Define \(p(P')=(p_j(P'))_{j\in\mathcal J}\) and \(\omega(P')=(\omega_j(P'))_{j\in\mathcal J}\) by \(p_j(P')=P'\{(D,Z)=c_j\}\) and \(\omega_j(P')=\mathbb E_{P'}[\mathbf 1\{(D,Z)=c_j\}(Y-\ell_{d_j})/(u_{d_j}-\ell_{d_j})]\). Because \(d_j\in\{d,e\}\) and \(Y\in[\ell_{D},u_D]\) almost surely, these are unconditional bounded moments satisfying \(0\le\omega_j(P')\le p_j(P')\); they require no conditional-mean division.
